Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘great doubt.’ The phrase occurs 196 times in 91 allowlisted texts. A direct definition says, ‘doubt has no large or small; only when the doubt is weighty is it called great doubt, and when light it is called small doubt’ (疑情無大小，但疑之重，是謂大疑；疑之輕，是謂小疑). The same record says that when one cannot refrain from raising it, ‘therefore it is named great doubt.’ Across other texts it appears in the fixed contrast ‘great doubt, great awakening; small doubt, small awakening; no doubt, no awakening,’ in questions about ‘a person of great doubt,’ and in biographies where a master ‘greatly doubted’ after an exchange or saying. Thus the corpus uses the phrase both as a named weight of doubt and verbally for becoming deeply doubtful; English ‘great doubt’ covers both without positing different referents.
Senses.Note: Zen bends an ordinary degree phrase by making it a named category explicitly defined against small doubt and repeatedly paired with great awakening. The family comparison with ‘doubt-mass’ (疑情) and ‘ball of doubt’ (疑團) supports one sense, not a noun/verb split: both constructions name the same doubt.

Occurrences.Kwic: 但疑之重，是謂大疑；疑之輕，是謂小疑
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Miscellaneous Records of Tianmu Mingben (天目明本禪師雜錄): in his instruction to Chan student Yi, Zhongfeng Mingben defines heavy doubt as great doubt and light doubt as small doubt.

Occurrences.Kwic: 信根若具，便起大疑心；疑心若起，便得大悟門。所以云：大疑大悟，小疑小悟，不疑不悟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai (無異元來禪師廣錄), complete hall address by Wuyi Yuanlai: Wuyi states the fixed contrast of great doubt and great awakening, small doubt and small awakening, and no doubt and no awakening.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。如何是大疑底人。師曰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): inside Fenghuang Congchen Hongren's section, an unnamed monk asks what a person of great doubt is; Fenghuang Congchen Hongren supplies the answer. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not give a personal name for the unnamed questioning monk.

The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Xiuyun Wei's explicitly headed biography, Xiuyun Wei is the grammatical actor who comes into great doubt and investigates with fierce effort.
